Title: Better welfare support needed for rural healthcare workers in Sabah
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Better welfare support is needed to encourage doctors and healthcare workers to remain in rural and remote areas of Sabah, said Sabah Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) chairman Dr Brandon Patrick Senagang.
He said while the government's efforts to repair and upgrade health clinics, district hospitals and other healthcare facilities were welcomed, the welfare of the doctors and healthcare workers serving in them should not be overlooked.
His call followed a town hall session with doctors in Keningau, including those serving in several rural and remote areas.
"What struck me most was meeting doctors from Peninsular Malaysia who have chosen to continue serving in rural Sabah for more than five years.
"They were not talking about wanting to leave Sabah. On the contrary, many shared that they were happy working here. They spoke warmly of supportive colleagues, welcoming local communities and patients who genuinely appreciate their service," he said.
However, Dr Brandon said the lack of suitable and adequate staff quarters was repeatedly raised as a concern.
Rental accommodation was extremely limited or unavailable in some rural areas, while existing staff quarters were sometimes insufficient, old or dilapidated and in need of comprehensive repairs.
"As a result, some doctors are forced to live far from their place of work and commute long distances every day. Such journeys not only add financial cost and physical fatigue, but over time can also affect the physical and mental well-being of healthcare workers," he said.
Those challenges were compounded by gaps in basic infrastructure in some areas, including interruptions to water and electricity supplies and poor road conditions.
He said the Sabah Government could assist by identifying or allocating suitable land for the development of healthcare staff quarters and improving roads, water supply, electricity, telecommunications and other basic amenities.
"We often speak about the shortage of doctors in Sabah, particularly in rural and remote areas.
"Financial incentives and allowances may have a role to play, but a doctor's decision to remain in a particular area is also influenced by very basic considerations - do they have a safe place to live? Can their family live comfortably? Is the water and electricity supply reliable? Is the journey to work reasonable?" he said.
He added that retaining doctors in rural districts would also benefit patients through greater continuity of care, as doctors who stayed longer could build stronger relationships with communities and develop a deeper understanding of local health challenges.
"They are not asking for luxury. They are asking for the basics - a safe and suitable place to live, reliable water and electricity, and reasonable road access that allows them to carry out their work properly," he said.
"Caring for the welfare of those who care for the health of our people is not merely an expense. It is an investment in the long-term sustainability of rural healthcare services in Sabah."

Title: Anwar: Wrongdoing at Tabung Haji, Felda must face action regardless of race
Article:
BANGI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said allegations of wrongdoing involving Tabung Haji and Felda must be dealt with firmly, stressing that action should be taken regardless of whether those involved are Malay- or Muslim-linked.
Anwar said governance and management weaknesses should not be turned into racial or religious issues, adding that Muslims should instead be held to a higher standard of ethics, integrity and accountability.
"We do not ask whether the company is Malay or Muslim. If there is a problem, we take action. In fact, if you ask me, Muslims must be even more serious and meticulous when it comes to ethics, management and values," he said at a session with Felda leadership and management here today.

Title: Jardine Cycle & Carriage is selling its Malaysian, Singaporean business to Indonesia's Chandra Asri
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Jardine Cycle & Carriage Ltd (JC&C) is selling its Cycle & Carriage automotive businesses in Malaysia and Singapore to Indonesia's Chandra Asri Group for S$265 million (about US$207 million).
According to the company's announcement on the Singapore Exchange, JC&C said the transaction is aimed at improving shareholder returns through active portfolio management and disciplined capital allocation.
It said the proposed sale covers JC&C's the distribution and retail of new and used vehicles, as well as aftersales, financing and insurance services.
"Overall, the proposed transaction enables JC&C to crystallise value from the Cycle & Carriage business as we focus on our core markets of Indonesia and Vietnam and deliver a positive outcome for shareholders, while positioning Cycle & Carriage for continued success under its new owner," it said in the bourse filing.
JC&C said Cycle & Carriage would be well-positioned within the Chandra Asri Group ecosystem to leverage synergies and collaboration opportunities, strengthening its competitiveness and supporting future growth.
The assets being sold had a book value and net tangible asset value of about US$292million as at June 30,2026,and contributed approximately US$16 million in net profit for the first half of 2026.
Chandra Asri Group is an Indonesia-listed energy, chemicals and infrastructure solutions provider.
Its principal shareholders include PT Barito Pacific Tbk and its affiliates, SCG Chemicals Public Co Ltd and Thai Oil Public Co Ltd.
The transaction is expected to be completed by Feb 28, 2027, subject to the fulfilment or waiver of the conditions under the agreement.
The Malaysian arm of Cycle & Carriage was previously listed on Bursa Malaysia's Main Market under Cycle & Carriage Bintang Bhd before being taken private by JC&C and delisted on Sept 19, 2022, at RM2.70 per share.
In 2018, Cycle & Carriage Bintang sold its 49 per cent stake in Mercedes-Benz Malaysia, the distributor of Mercedes vehicles, to Daimler AG, the parent company of Mercedes-Benz, for RM66 million in 2018.
It currently operates 12 outlets across key markets in Peninsular Malaysia and is an authorised Mercedes-Benz dealer and service provider, as well as a dealer for Peugeot and Leapmotor. It also provides sales and after-sales services for Fuso trucks.

Title: Bersatu must repair PN ties ahead of GE16, says Perlis MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu must mend ties with its Perikatan Nasional (PN) partners and review its strategy ahead of the 16th General Election (GE16), said Perlis Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah.
According to Utusan Malaysia, Abu Bakar said Bersatu needed to recognise that it could not succeed without being part of a political coalition, warning that going solo in GE16 would make victory "impossible".
"Looking at Bersatu's future, the party needs to review several actions, including issues involving the expulsion of its members and its relationship with PN component parties.
"What is certain is that if Bersatu goes solo, it will be impossible for the party to win. Bersatu must be part of a coalition," he said.
Abu Bakar said the party leadership could have its own plans for political cooperation or be exploring other options, but any decision would depend on the prevailing political situation.
On Perlis, he said Bersatu remained part of PN unless the party's central leadership decided otherwise.
He added that Bersatu elected representatives remained bound by the anti-party-hopping law, with any decision on the party's future to be made after the state legislative assembly is dissolved.
Earlier, Abu Bakar said cooperation within
PN remained intact
among Pas, Bersatu, Gerakan, Pejuang and Malaysian Indian People's Party (MIPP), with no decision by the coalition's Supreme Council to the contrary.
Abu Bakar, who is the state's party chairman and Kangar division chief,
resigned from the Bersatu
Supreme Council on July 9.

Title: Pahang retiree loses RM81,465 to online 'lover' he never met
Article:
MARAN: A retiree realised he had fallen victim to a love scam after his partner failed to turn up for their first meeting, by which time he had lost RM81,465.
The man, in his 60s, had deposited the money after the woman claimed she needed financial assistance for various personal expenses, including buying jewellery and repairing her car.
Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said the victim claimed he was in a relationship with the woman, whom he had befriended on June 13 this year.
"The woman sought financial assistance, giving various excuses, including needing money to pay her room rental, repair her car, purchase jewellery and for personal use.
"The victim made 44 transactions amounting to RM81,465 into six separate bank accounts between June 13 and Aug 7. The woman promised to meet the victim on Aug 10," he said in a statement today.
Wong said the man went to the planned location to meet the woman, but she failed to turn up.
"When he contacted her, the woman gave various excuses. The victim then realised that he had been cheated and lodged a police report," he said.
The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating, which carries a jail term of between one and 10 years, whipping and a fine upon conviction.

Title: TM's data centre bet pays off as Nxera hits 70pct take-up
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Telekom Malaysia Bhd's (TM) data centre business is gaining traction, with about 70 per cent of the capacity at its TM Nxera data centre joint venture already contracted ahead of the first phase coming online next month.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) analyst Toh Woo Kim said the initial 20 megawatts (MW) of the 64MW Phase 1 capacity is expected to be ready for service by September, with the remaining 44MW scheduled for the first quarter of 2027.
"TM's newly expanded Iskandar Puteri data centre capacity is fully taken up, with customers progressively moving in towards year-end," he said.
Toh said TM's management was already in discussions on subsequent expansion phases after securing 280MW of power for the entire site.
RHB Research analyst Jeffrey Tan said TM's data centre business remained under-appreciated, with the brokerage expecting the segment to deliver double-digit revenue and earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation growth in financial year 2027 (FY27) and FY28.
"Management said about 70 per cent of the capacity at TM Nxera, the 51:49 artificial intelligence data centre joint venture with Singtel, has been pre-sold," Tan said in a note.
RHB Research estimated that TM could receive RM50 million to RM60 million a year in earnings contribution from TM Nxera as an associate, translating into about a two per cent uplift to TM's FY27 and FY28 earnings and around 16 sen per share in equity value accretion.
Against the backdrop of its data centre expansion, both brokerages maintained their positive views on TM following its second-quarter results.
TM's core profit after tax and minority interest rose 4.6 per cent year-on-year to RM406 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, while core earnings for the first half grew eight per cent to RM843 million.
HLIB said the first-half core earnings were broadly in line with expectations, accounting for 45 per cent of its full-year forecast and 49 per cent of consensus estimates, given TM's seasonally stronger second half.
Revenue increased 6.8 per cent year-on-year to RM2.96 billion in the second quarter, driven by growth across consumer-to-consumer, business-to-consumer and business-to-business segments.
For the first half, revenue rose 4.8 per cent to RM5.9 billion, while core earnings before interest and tax declined 3.7 per cent to RM1.19 billion after adjusting for costs including FIFA World Cup-related expenses.
HLIB noted that Unifi recorded modest subscriber growth, with net additions rising to 3,000 in the second quarter from 1,000 in the first quarter, bringing its subscriber base to 3.23 million.
Average revenue per user held at RM132 a month, supported by higher-tier migration, device bundling and FIFA-linked content.
RHB noted that TM One's revenue grew two per cent in the first half, its strongest growth in more than four years, while TM Global's revenue increased seven per cent.
The firm expects stronger wholesale revenue from the data centre expansion and the commissioning of the Asean Link Cable in the second quarter of 2027.
TM also completed its exit from Digital Nasional Bhd's 5G network on July 31 and began using the second 5G network in August, which RHB expects to generate direct cost savings.
HLIB maintained its "Buy" call on TM but raised its target price to RM9.10 from RM8.60.
RHB also kept its "Buy" call with a RM9.30 target price, citing structural growth drivers and cost discipline that could support a 14 per cent compound annual growth rate in core earnings between FY26 and FY28.

Title: Former TH CEO remanded 7 days over RCI report
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A former chief executive officer of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has been remanded for seven days in connection with the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into TH.
The remand order, which runs until Aug 27, was issued by magistrate Ezrene Zakariah after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) made an application at the Putrajaya magistrates' court this morning.
The 60-something-year-old man, wearing orange lock-up attire and handcuffs, arrived at 9.38am accompanied by MACC officers.
BH reported yesterday that he was believed to be among the latest individuals being investigated by MACC in connection with the RCI report on TH.
A source had previously said the individual was also a prominent corporate figure who had held positions in several leading companies in the country.
BH has sought confirmation from the MACC chief commissioner on the matter.
MACC had previously detained and called in seven people to assist in investigations into the RCI report.
They included a former chief executive officer of a shipping company, a director of a construction company, a former company director and four former senior TH management personnel.
The RCI report on TH, which was made public after four years, put forward 25 key recommendations aimed at enhancing transparency, professionalism and governance at the institution.
Among the key recommendations was a proposal to bar active politicians from serving on TH's board of directors to prevent political interference.
His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had also decreed that the investigation into the RCI report be conducted "until every stone is turned".

Title: Anwar condemns Israeli tender for E1 settlement project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has condemned Israel's decision to issue construction tenders for the E1 settlement project east of Jerusalem, saying the move would undermine the prospect of a contiguous Palestinian state.
Anwar said the tract of land had long been critical to the viability of a Palestinian state, adding that construction there would divide the West Bank.
"I unreservedly denounce the Israeli regime's decision to issue construction tenders for the E1 settlement project.
"This tract of land east of Jerusalem has long been critical to the viability of a Palestinian state. Building on it would divide the West Bank and gravely undermine the prospect of a contiguous Palestinian homeland," he said in a statement.
Anwar said Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank were illegal under international law, but Israel continued to act with what he described as "utter impunity".
He said the decision, which came amid settler violence against Palestinian civilians in the West Bank and the ongoing war in Gaza, showed that Israel had abandoned even the pretence of seeking peace or respecting the will of the international community.
"Malaysia stands staunchly with the Palestinian people and their inalienable right to a sovereign, viable, contiguous and independent Palestinian state.
"Malaysia will take careful note of any international company that chooses to participate in these tenders and will act accordingly," he said.

Title: Lee Lam Thye calls for tougher penalties for red-light runners
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Veteran social activist and Road Safety Council member Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye has called on the government to consider amending relevant road traffic laws to impose more severe penalties on red-light runners.
He said stiffer penalties would send a clear message that traffic signals must be respected in the interest of everyone's safety.
"Speeding and beating the traffic light is the most serious offence. I really hope the government consider amending the road traffic ordinance to provide for a more severe penalty against those who beat the red lights.
"As a progressive, this nation, I think everyone must bear in mind that laws are meant to be followed," he said.
Lee also lauded the statement made by Federal Police Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department director Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali that
flashing beacon lights
and blaring sirens did not give enforcement or emergency vehicle drivers a licence to run red lights.
Lee said the same principle applied to emergency vehicles, whose drivers should exercise extra caution when approaching intersections despite responding to emergencies.
"I think it is very clear, there's no excuse. Even government vehicles, just like any ordinary vehicles, have to follow the law, they have to follow regulations and they have to ensure that if there is a red light, there's a red light.
"Ambulances for example, when it comes to the intersection with the red light they have to be extra cautious in order to avoid any untoward incidents," he said.
Lee said Malaysia should not accept the loss of about 6,000 lives on the roads each year as normal.
"If we are going to move forward as a progressive nation, everyone must bear in mind that laws are meant to be complied with and followed. Speeding and beating traffic lights are among the most serious offences.
"Road safety is a shared responsibility. It is everyone's responsibility, and I really hope that all road users will embrace this road safety culture," he said.
On Thursday,
three family members, including a 12-year-old girl, were killed
after an Immigration Department truck allegedly ran a red light, struck a car and ploughed into pedestrians along Jalan Sultan Ismail.
The victims, a 53-year-old man and his two daughters aged 25 and 12, died at the scene following the 1am crash at the Maju Junction traffic light intersection.
The man's 55-year-old wife suffered head, hand and leg injuries and was rushed to Kuala Lumpur Hospital for treatment.

Title: Immigration busts love scam, counterfeit goods syndicate, 21 held
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Immigration Department has busted a syndicate running love scams and selling counterfeit goods to overseas victims, detaining 21 people in an operation at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) and Nilai, Negri Sembilan.
Immigration Department director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the operation was conducted on Wednesday following a month-long intelligence-gathering exercise and began at 5.55pm.
He said personnel from the department's Intelligence and Special Operations Division and Security and Passport Division were first deployed to KLIA Terminal 1, where they detained a local man believed to be a syndicate member and two Chinese nationals, a man and a woman aged between 50 and 53.
"Initial investigations found that the syndicate facilitated the entry of foreigners into Malaysia, including Chinese citizens believed to have been blacklisted by the Immigration Department.
"The two Chinese suspects were believed to possess two passports bearing different numbers, with the passport that was not blacklisted used to pass through the e-Gates at KLIA. The blacklisted Chinese passports were found in their bags during checks," he said in a statement.
The local suspect was believed to have been responsible for transporting the two Chinese citizens to designated locations for between RM150 and RM500 per person, depending on the destination.
Zakaria said the operation team also seized four Chinese passports, four mobile phones and a Proton X70 believed to have been used by the syndicate.
Following questioning, officers conducted a follow-up raid at a residential premises in Taman Desa Melati, Nilai, where they detained 18 more people, including four alleged masterminds.
"The four alleged masterminds comprised two Chinese men, a Chinese woman and a Russian woman.
"The remaining 14 detainees comprised nine Chinese men, a Vanuatu man, a Pakistani man, and women from China, India and Myanmar."
He said the foreign nationals detained at the premises were aged between 23 and 33 and had entered Malaysia using Social Visit Passes.
"A search of the premises uncovered 28 Chinese passports, as well as one passport each from Myanmar, India, Vanuatu and Russia.
"Department personnel also seized 11 desktop computers, laptops, 40 mobile phones and RM4,800 in cash believed to be proceeds from the syndicate's activities," he said.
Zakaria said the syndicate had been using luxury residential premises in secluded areas as operational bases for its online fraud activities.
"It used platforms such as Telegram and WhatsApp to deceive overseas victims through 'love scams' and the sale of counterfeit goods using prepared scripts.
"Members were paid commissions based on the number of victims they successfully deceived, and the syndicate is believed to have made profits of up to US$50,000 (RM210,000)," he said.
He said both activities were believed to have been operating since early this year.
The local syndicate member and four alleged masterminds were detained under Section 56(1)(d) of the Immigration Act 1959/63, while the other foreign nationals were detained under Section 15(1)(c) of the same Act and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.
All 21 detainees were brought to the Putrajaya Immigration Office for further action.

Title: Parkson back on investors' radar, shares jump nearly 19pct ahead of Q2 results
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Investors piled into Parkson Holdings Bhd ahead of its second-quarter earnings, sending the retailer's shares up nearly 19 per cent in their busiest trading in over a year.
The stock opened flat at 18.5 sen before rising as much as 3.5 sen, or 18.92 per cent, to 22 sen, nearing its year-high of 22.5 sen recorded on Jan 5.
At 11.17am, Parkson was trading at a six-month high of 21.5 sen, up three sen or 16.22 per cent, with 22.64 million shares changing hands. It was the sixth most actively traded stock on Bursa Malaysia.
At 21.5 sen, the retail group and department-store operator had a market capitalisation of RM247.01 million.
There were no fresh corporate developments involving Parkson, with its latest Bursa Malaysia filing on July 24 concerning the dissolution of two dormant subsidiaries.
The company is due to release its second-quarter results this month.
For the first quarter ended March 31, 2026, Parkson's net profit rose 37.4 per cent to RM41.42 million from RM30.14 million a year earlier, boosted by improved profitability in China and its other businesses despite weaker retail sales.
Revenue fell 10 per cent to RM692.81 million from RM769.48 million, mainly due to weaker sales in China as consumers remained cautious amid macroeconomic headwinds and muted income growth expectations.
Parkson currently has no fundamental analyst coverage, according to MyBursa.

Title: Australia investigates fourth close call at Sydney airport in less than a month
Article:
SYDNEY: Australia's transport safety regulator said on Friday it had launched an investigation into a fourth incident involving air traffic control at Sydney airport in less than a month after two planes were directed towards the same intersection on the ground.
A Qantas Airbus A321 preparing to depart to the Gold Coast braked to avoid another Qantas aircraft, a Boeing 737, that had arrived from Melbourne on Tuesday, the Australian Transport Safety Bureau said in a statement.
The Boeing had been cleared to continue along a taxiway that the Airbus had been cleared to turn onto, it said.
The ATSB said there was no immediate risk of collision, but had launched an investigation to understand if there were any contributing factors in common with three other incidents at the airport over the last month.
"The evidence collection phase of the investigation will involve interviewing involved air traffic controllers and flight crew, retrieving and reviewing available recorded data, and the collection of other relevant information," the ATSB said.
A preliminary report is expected in six to eight weeks.
On July 27, two Qantas aircraft narrowly avoided a collision after a QantasLink Dash 8 completing a landing and a Qantas 737 whose pilots reported they had been cleared to cross the same runway came into conflict. The 737 was able to stop, though only after crossing the safety hold point.
On Aug 9, a Jetstar A320 had to brake suddenly on the tarmac to avoid colliding with a Qatar Airways Boeing 777, injuring a cabin crew member.
The same day, a Virgin Australia 737 cleared for takeoff spotted a Qantas aircraft crossing the runway ahead and stopped about 1km (0.62 miles) short of the other plane, which had also been cleared to cross.
Separately, the ATSB said on Thursday it had received a report from an air traffic controller that staff at the airport had been unprepared for complex airspace and procedure changes resulting from the opening of a new international airport in the city's west.
The report, made in early June, said more than 50 controllers at the airport had responded to a union survey, with most expressing concern at the lack of time given to learn "an enormous amount of highly detailed and complex material" before the airspace changes came into effect on July 9.
The controller raised concerns of similarities to the air traffic control situation in Washington, D.C., ahead of a deadly mid-air collision in January 2025 where staff had pleaded with local management for changes in the months leading up to the accident.
In response, Australia's Civil Aviation Safety Authority, which investigated the report, found that Airservices Australia, the government entity employing air traffic controllers, had implemented appropriate training, procedures and operational support arrangements relating to the changes.

Title: NexG, NexG Bina shares surge on government buyout prospect
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Shares of NexG Bhd and its associate NexG Bina Bhd surged in active trade after NexG confirmed that the government had sought an indicative price for a possible acquisition of its wholly owned subsidiary Datasonic Technologies Sdn Bhd (DTSB).
NexG emerged as Bursa Malaysia's most actively traded counter after trading resumed at 10am today, following a one-hour suspension after the opening bell.
The stock opened 1.5 sen, or 4.5 per cent, higher at 34.5 sen, with more than 62 million shares changing hands, its busiest trading in more than eight months. At that price, the company was valued at about RM1.28 billion.
NexG Bina, formerly known as Classita Holdings Bhd, was the third most actively traded counter, rising half a sen, or 16.67 per cent, to 3.5 sen, valuing it at about RM43 million. More than 22 million shares changed hands, its heaviest trading in over two months.
NexG Bina became an associate of NexG after the latter acquired a 32.61 per cent stake in the company in August 2025.
Meanwhile, MMAG Holdings Bhd, in which NexG holds a 9.48 per cent stake, went the other way, falling half a sen, or 16.67 per cent, to 2.5 sen, on thin volume of 758,400 shares.
The buying interest followed NexG's clarification yesterday over the government's approach concerning DTSB, its core operating business and main contributor to group revenue and earnings.
NexG said the Finance Ministry verbally conveyed the request during a meeting with DTSB on July 24, with no written document issued.
The ministry had asked DTSB to assess three potential scenarios — compensation that may be payable if its MyKad supply contract is terminated, an indicative price for the possible acquisition of DTSB and an indicative price for the possible acquisition of a controlling block in NexG.
NexG said its management had internally assessed DTSB's indicative value at about RM7.5 billion using the discounted cash flow method.
The assessment took into account DTSB's future earnings-generating capabilities, projected cash flows, business sustainability and other factors affecting its operations.
However, NexG stressed that the RM7.5 billion figure was solely an internal assessment and did not constitute an independent valuation, an agreed transaction value or a firm offer.
Any potential deal remains subject to further discussions and negotiations between the relevant parties, as well as an independent valuation where appropriate, it added.
With DTSB at the heart of NexG's operations, the company said any disposal, if it materialises, could have a material impact on the group's operations and financial performance and potentially affect its continued listing status on Bursa Malaysia's Main Market.
NexG said it would comply with applicable listing requirements and seek the necessary approvals from shareholders, Bursa Malaysia and other relevant authorities should the proposed transaction proceed.
The company had said on Thursday that the RM7.5 billion indicative value took into account DTSB's intellectual property and about RM1.9 billion in committed investments for the current national identity programme.
DTSB holds a RM1.73 billion contract to supply passport booklets and polycarbonate biodata pages to the Immigration Department from June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2032.
It also has a RM732.72 million contract to supply raw cards and consumables to the National Registration Department over the same period.
NexG said DTSB owns intellectual property related to biometric identity verification, MyKad and passport technologies, including systems involving facial recognition and multimodal biometrics.
DTSB has also committed investments in personnel, equipment, system upgrades and two manufacturing plants in Petaling Jaya and Meru.
NexG said it would make further announcements should there be material developments concerning the possible transaction.

Title: 2 cyclists killed in Putrajaya road crash
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Two cyclists were killed after being hit by a car at Km9 nine of Jalan Persiaran Selatan here last night.
Putrajaya district police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed said preliminary investigations found that the car, driven by a man in his 40s, had changed lanes from the middle lane to the left lane before hitting both victims at about 10.15pm.
"The victims, aged in their 40s and 30s respectively, were confirmed dead at the scene," he said in a statement today.
Aidi Sham said both victims suffered serious injuries to their faces and heads.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
"Members of the public or witnesses with information are urged to come forward to assist investigations by contacting the Putrajaya Traffic Police Station at 03-8886 2138 or any nearby police station," he said.

Title: Missing angler found drowned after three-day search in Sungai Pahang
Article:
TEMERLOH: An angler who was reported missing after falling into Sungai Pahang at Kampung Lebak Seberang while fishing on Aug 19 was found drowned today.
The remains of Muhamed Hanifa Mammu, 47, were found at about 7.05am, some 150m from where he was last seen.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department public relations officer Zulfadli Zakaria said the search and rescue operation, which entered its third day today, involved six firefighters scouring the area where the victim was last seen.
"The operation began at 6.50am, and the victim was found less than 20 minutes later. His remains were handed over to the police," he said in a statement today.
In the incident at about 11pm on Aug 19, the victim was fishing at the river when he fell into the water before villagers alerted the Fire and Rescue Department.
Firefighters from the Bukit Angin Fire and Rescue Station, along with divers from the department's underwater rescue team, were deployed to the river to assist in the search operation.

Title: Man held after threatening police with parang during raid
Article:
JELI: A man was arrested after he allegedly threatened to kill police personnel with a parang during a raid at a house in Kampung Lubok Bongor here yesterday.
Jeli district police chief Superintendent Kamarulzaman Harun said a team from the district Criminal Investigation Division conducted the raid at 11am following public tip-offs.
"During the raid, the suspect became aggressive and allegedly pulled out a 36cm-long parang from his waist before pointing it at the policemen and threatening to kill them.
"While attempting to arrest the suspect, a struggle broke out between him and the police personnel.
"One policeman sustained injuries to his left middle finger and left shoulder.
"The suspect was later arrested," he said.
Kamarulzaman said police also seized the parang and a transparent plastic packet containing six pills suspected to be yaba, which were found inside a black waist bag.
"Initial investigations found that the suspect was wanted by the Jeli Narcotics Criminal Investigation Division for allegedly being actively involved in drug trafficking in the district.
"He was also wanted in connection with an earlier incident on Aug 19, in which he allegedly threatened to kill police personnel while wielding a parang during a police raid," he added.
The case is being investigated under Sections 324 and 353 of the Penal Code and Section 12(2) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
The suspect will be brought before the court to obtain a remand order under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code to facilitate further investigations.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Asia shares downbeat on the week as bond yields, oil stay high
Article:
SYDNEY: Most Asian share indices were heading for weekly falls on Friday as stress in global bond markets showed little sign of abating, while a diplomatic deadlock in the Gulf lifted oil prices to one-month highs and kept inflation risks to the fore.
Yields on US Treasuries had resumed their climb after Wednesday's surprise intervention by Treasury brought barely a day of relief from selling.
The rise came even as US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he could further increase the government's repurchases of Treasuries, and floated the idea of fiscal consolidation.
Analysts were sceptical he could find enough spending cuts to seriously curb a budget deficit of more than 6 per cent of gross domestic product, with interest charges alone this year running at US$1.2 trillion.
"Historically, markets have pushed back when they believe fundamentals – like record debt level and historically large deficits – are on their side, and further interventions could become too costly to bear," cautioned Steven Zeng, a strategist at Deutsche Bank.
"There is also the potential cost to Treasury's institutional credibility if its activist approach erodes some of the goodwill and benefits that have been built over the years by adhering to a regular and predictable framework," he added.
Investors showed their scepticism by nudging 30-year bond yields back up to 5.25 per cent, while the 10-year hit 4.71 per cent. Markets assume 5.30 per cent is now a pain threshold for Treasury, much like the 160.00 yen level has become for Japanese policymakers.
Higher yields lift debt costs globally, just as tech giants are borrowing heavily to fund AI capex, while raising the discount on corporate earnings and challenging stock valuations.
The strain was evident in the Nikkei which slipped 0.8 per cent, bringing losses for the week so far to 4.4 per cent. South Korea and Taiwan both edged higher, but again were down on the week.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan added 0.5 per cent.
In Europe, EUROSTOXX 50 futures and DAX futures were a fraction lower, while FTSE futures dipped 0.1 per cent. On Wall Street, a bumper earnings season has provided some support with S&P 500 futures up 0.1 per cent, while Nasdaq futures gained 0.2 per cent.
The entire AI trade faces a huge hurdle next week when Nvidia reports, with much riding on its outlook for infrastructure demand and data centre revenue.
Walmart on Thursday showed what happens when high expectations are disappointed, sliding 9 per cent on a sales miss.
WARFARE AND DEBASEMENT
Bessent also made news by expanding on President Donald Trump's pledge of economic warfare against Iran, saying the US would impose "the toughest sanctions in history" on the country.
The threats further dimmed hopes for a deal that would fully open the vital Strait of Hormuz and pushed Brent to a one-month top of US$94.71, before profit-taking set in.
Brent futures were last off 0.7 per cent at US$93.12 a barrel, but still up more than 5 per cent for the week, while US crude eased 0.7 per cent to US$86.18 a barrel.
In currency markets, the dollar was nursing broad losses for the week amid worries ever-growing US debt and policy uncertainties will erode the purchasing power of the currency, driving investors to scarce assets including gold.
The yellow metal was steady at US$4,513 an ounce, having climbed 3.1 per cent for the week so far.
"The dollar has come under renewed pressure, in part due to a resurgent 'debasement' narrative," said Jonas Goltermann, chief markets economist at Capital Economics.
"While we continue to think such concerns are somewhat overblown, and that the economic backdrop overall will point to a stronger dollar over the coming months, continued surprises from US policymakers may well matter more in the near term."
The dollar index was off almost 0.9 per cent for the week at 98.802 , having hit a three-month trough overnight. The euro was up 1.0 per cent on the week at US$1.1686, after touching a 14-week peak.
The dollar fared better on the yen, which has plenty of problems of its own, and held at 159.07.
Data showed Japan's core consumer inflation accelerated in July as firms passed on rising import costs, adding to the case for a September rate hike from the Bank of Japan.
Markets, however, are already priced for a quarter-point rise to 1.25 per cent and would really like a commitment to faster and more aggressive tightening from policy makers.

Title: Sarawak closes 591 schools as haze worsens
Article:
KUCHING: A total of 591 schools in Sarawak were closed today as air quality deteriorated amid transboundary haze, with the API in Serian reaching 242.
Data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System portal showed that, as of 6am, the API reading in Serian, near the Malaysia-Indonesia border, had reached 242, categorised as very unhealthy.
Eight other areas in Sarawak also recorded API readings, namely Sri Aman (189), Kuching (188), Samarahan (180), Sarikei (172), Sibu (156), Bintulu (153), Samalaju (36) and Kapit (107).
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.
Following deteriorating air quality due to transboundary haze, 591 schools under the supervision of 10 District Education Offices in Sarawak were closed today.
The Sarawak Education Department, in a statement yesterday, said the closure involved 509 primary schools with a total of 107,590 pupils and 82 secondary schools involving 89,733 students.
The schools are under the supervision of the Kuching, Padawan, Bau, Lundu, Samarahan, Simunjan, Serian, Sri Aman, Lubok Antu and Betong District Education Offices.

Title: Oil set for second weekly rise as unsettled US-Iran war crimps supply
Article:
SINGAPORE: Oil prices were little changed on Friday, but were on track for a second weekly rise as the stalemated US-Iran war continues to disrupt supply from the key Middle East producing region.
Brent crude futures rose 4 cents to US$93.82 a barrel by 0142 GMT, after climbing 2.4 per cent in the previous session. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures slipped 6 cents to US$86.78 a barrel, after climbing 2.3 per cent in the prior session.
During the previous five days of gains, Brent gained more than 7 per cent and WTI climbed more than 8 per cent, reaching their highest since July 24.
Prices have climbed on concerns the inconclusive state of the US-Israeli war on Iran will mean the continued curtailment of supply from major oil producers such as Saudi Arabia, Iraq, the UAE and Kuwait.
The earlier peace deal between them expired this week with no effort by either side to restart talks and US President Donald Trump threatened economic retaliation against nations supporting Iran.
"Both sides are dug in but lacking the luxury of time to play the waiting game, against a backdrop of crude prices grinding unerringly higher," IG analyst Tony Sycamore said on Friday.
On Wednesday evening, Trump threatened "economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale" against Tehran, warning of consequences for any country that provided "any type of lifeline to Iran".
This week, the United Arab Emirates suspended all financial and economic transactions with Iran until further notice, highlighting the fraught ties between the major Gulf Arab oil producer and Tehran.
Thousands of people have been killed in the Iran war, which began on February 28 when the US and Israel launched military strikes on Iran. Since then, Tehran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian attacks on energy facilities across the Middle East have disrupted global oil and gas flows.
Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday was unchanged from the day before with nine vessel transiting the waterway, far below pre-war levels. Prior to the Iran war, shipments equal to about one-fifth of global consumption moved through the waterway.

Title: Dollar wobbles as investors balk at US Treasury's rescue efforts
Article:
SINGAPORE: The dollar was on shaky ground and set for a weekly loss on Friday, as investors viewed the US Treasury's bond buyback gambit as merely a temporary fix, while raising fresh concerns about officials' increasingly interventionist approach.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said overnight he may further increase the government's repurchases of Treasuries, a day after the department announced it would double the size of buybacks on longer-dated securities over the next quarter in an attempt to stem a sharp rise in yields.
Bessent also said he and White House budget director Russell Vought will be embarking on a new fiscal consolidation effort directed by US President Donald Trump.
The moves, however, did little to stem the selloff in US Treasuries and weighed on the dollar, as investors grew wary of the deteriorating fiscal picture and worries about the credibility of US institutions resurfaced.
Against a weaker dollar, the euro was perched near a three-month high and last bought US$1.1685, on track for a weekly rise of 1 per cent.
Sterling flirted with a six-month peak and edged 0.08 per cent higher to US$1.3643, taking its gains for the week thus far to 0.8 per cent.
The greenback was meanwhile on track for a weekly fall of more than 0.8 per cent and was last at 98.82, languishing near a three-month low against a basket of six other currencies.
"The Treasury's long bond buybacks are basically another example of the US government using unconventional tools to manage borrowing costs, and this comes against the backdrop of high government debt, growing fiscal deficits and policy uncertainty," said Carol Kong, a currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
"So I can understand why people are concerned about the operation being another headwind to investor sentiment around US dollar assets. Potentially we could see such an action encourage more dollar hedging and diversification."
In other currencies, the Australian dollar advanced 0.13 per cent to US$0.7123, while the New Zealand dollar added 0.23 per cent to US$0.5957 and was headed for a weekly rise of more than 1 per cent.
The yen slipped 0.05 per cent to 159.12 per dollar, continuing to come under pressure from wide US-Japan rate differentials.
Data on Friday showed Japan's core consumer inflation accelerated in July from a year earlier, bolstering the case for a rate hike from the central bank.
JUST A BAND-AID
The yield on the 30-year US Treasury note was up about 1.4 basis points to 5.2508 per cent on Friday, while the benchmark 10-year yield steadied at 4.7041 per cent after rising 4.5 bps overnight, as initial relief from Bessent's bond buyback plan faded.
"Our scepticism is not that policymakers lack the tools to influence the long end. History shows they do, at least temporarily. Our scepticism is that today's problem appears increasingly fiscal rather than technical," said Goldman Sachs strategist Vitali Meschoulam in a client note.
"The (developed market) examples tell us that term premia can be compressed. The (emerging market) examples tell us that once markets focus on sovereign financing dynamics, yield suppression becomes progressively less effective."
Concerns over the growing US debt pile, which has topped US$40 trillion, also drove some investors towards alternatives such as gold and bitcoin, which have benefitted in the past from efforts to diversify away from US assets.
Bitcoin scaled an over two-month high on Friday and last traded 1.6 per cent higher at US$73,823.43, on track for a 17 per cent weekly rise, which would mark its largest gain in 2-1/2 years.
Spot gold was similarly headed for a more than 3 per cent jump this week.

Title: Gold steadies, heads for third straight weekly gain
Article:
NEW YORK: Gold held steady on Friday but was on track for a third straight weekly gain, buoyed by a weaker dollar and US Treasury Department efforts to hold down longer-term yields.
Spot gold was little changed at US$4,514.23 per ounce, as of 0031 GMT, after hitting its highest level since early June in the previous session. Prices were up 3.2 per cent for the week.
US gold futures steadied at US$4,571.20. * The US dollar was headed for a weekly loss, making dollar-priced commodities cheaper for holders of other currencies.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Thursday he may further increase the government's repurchases of Treasuries. The Treasury on Wednesday announced that it would double the size of buybacks on longer-dated securities over the next quarter to at least US$4 billion per operation.
Two Federal Reserve officials expressed caution when asked how the Treasury Department's debt management changes could affect the US central bank's monetary policy choices.
Data showed the number of Americans filing claims for unemployment benefits slipped last week, suggesting that the labor market remains stable despite a surprise drop in employment in July and leaving the Fed in a position to keep its focus on containing inflation.
Markets are pricing in a 64 per cent chance that the Fed will keep rates unchanged in September and a 36 per cent chance of a hike, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.
Although gold is regarded as a hedge against turmoil and inflation, higher interest rates weigh on its appeal as a non-yielding asset.
On the geopolitical front, Bessent said the United States will impose "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran, a move he suggested would lessen the need for new major military operations.
Among other metals, spot silver was flat at US$68.03 per ounce. Platinum rose 01.1 per cent to US$1,846.29, while palladium steadied at US$1,333.11. All three metals headed for weekly gains.

Title: [UPDATED] Hong Kong Tiananmen activists found guilty of inciting subversion
Article:
HONG KONG: A Hong Kong court found on Friday two activists who organised annual vigils marking China's deadly Tiananmen crackdown in 1989 guilty of "incitement to subversion".
Lee Cheuk-yan, 69, and Chow Hang-tung, 41, "incited other persons to organise, plan, commit or participate in acts by unlawful means with a view to subverting the state power", a press summary handed out to reporters said.
A three-judge panel said they found both defendants had committed acts that constituted "overthrowing or undermining the basic system... established by the Constitution" of China.
They face a maximum penalty of 10 years in jail, with sentencing expected at a later date.
Lee and Chow were charged with subversion crimes in 2021 and have been behind bars since, under a Beijing-imposed national security law.
On Friday, they sat silently in the dock as the judges returned their verdict.
Hong Kong and Macau used to be the only places on Chinese soil that permitted public vigils to mourn those who died on June 4, 1989, when Beijing sent troops and tanks to crush protests calling for political reform in and around the capital's Tiananmen Square.
The defendants were leaders of the now-defunct Hong Kong Alliance, the group that organised annual vigils in the city's Victoria Park.
But public commemoration has been effectively banned since Beijing imposed a national security law on Hong Kong in 2020, following huge and sometimes violent pro-democracy protests the year before.
Prosecutors said the two leaders' remarks over the years were not merely expressions of personal opinion, "but were intended to incite others to commit unlawful acts".
They accused Lee and Chow in previous hearings of "endangering national security in the name of human rights", adding that freedom of speech and association are "not absolute rights".
A third defendant, 74-year-old former lawmaker Albert Ho, pleaded guilty in January. A guilty plea typically results in a reduced sentence.
Chow said in a blog post ahead of Friday's verdict that "justice lies in the hearts of the people, there is no need to revere judgments handed down from above, and a single verdict is of little consequence".
She added that since the trial began, prison officers have changed the way of escorting her.
"Rather than simply handcuffing, (I'm) now fully restrained with handcuffs, leg irons, a waist chain and a leg chain, and am led along by Correctional Services staff on a metal chain, much like a dog on a lead."

Title: Japan manufacturing expands as orders rise fastest since 2018, PMI shows
Article:
TOKYO: Japan's manufacturing sector expanded in August as new orders rose at their fastest pace since January 2018, a business survey showed on Friday.
The S&P Global Flash Japan Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in August from 54.5 in July, a preliminary estimate by S&P Global showed. The 50-mark separates growth from contraction.
"While we saw growth momentum pick up across both manufacturing and service sectors, factories continued to lead growth, registering sharp increases in both production and new orders," said Annabel Fiddes, economics associate director at S&P Global Market Intelligence.
Japan's economy slowed in the second ​quarter, gross domestic product data released on Monday showed, though investors brushed aside the soft reading as reflecting one-off factors.
Manufacturers also saw the steepest increase in total sales and overseas demand for more than 8-1/2 years, with firms citing strong demand from semiconductor and AI-related industries, Fiddes added.
Manufacturers led employment growth in August and expanded input buying, while stocks of purchases rose only slightly and suppliers' delivery times lengthened markedly.
Services activity also strengthened in August. The S&P Global Flash Japan Services PMI Business Activity Index rose to 52.3 from 51.2, helping lift the Composite Output Index to 53.4 from 52.7, its highest since February.
Cost pressures eased from June's near-record pace, with overall input inflation across the private sector slowing to a five-month low. Even so, selling prices for goods and services rose at one of the steepest rates on record.
Business confidence improved to its highest since February, with manufacturers more upbeat than services companies, attributing their optimism to expectations of higher sales, greater operational capacity and stronger overall market conditions.
"This adds to hopes that Japan's private sector remains well placed to perform strongly going forward, provided there are no further shocks to prices or demand," Fiddes said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former Tabung Haji CEO arrives at Putrajaya Court for remand hearing
Article:

Title: 14 Pontian landowners served notices over Singapore construction waste dumping
Article:
PONTIAN: Fourteen landowners whose properties were being used as dumping sites for construction waste from Singapore have been issued with notices by the Pontian Municipal Council (MPPn).
Council president Sulaiman Ismail said 11 of the 14 locations had been closed off, with notices placed at the entrances to the sites, reported Kosmo!.
He said most of the locations were in Mukim Sungai Karang, while several others were in Mukim Pontian, Mukim Jeram Batu/Pengkalan Raja and Mukim Serkat.
"MPPn will continue issuing notices at other locations to prevent those involved from carrying out similar activities.
"So far, 14 notices have been issued to landowners, while yellow tape has been placed at 11 locations, instructing them to stop all land reclamation works," he said when contacted by Kosmo! yesterday.
The notices were issued under Section 70A(1) of the Street, Drainage and Building Act 1974 (Act 133).
Kosmo! reported that Singapore had ordered all deliveries of construction and demolition (C&D) waste to Malaysia to be stopped immediately on Aug 18.
Meanwhile, resident Ahmad Daud Saeng, 59, welcomed the cooperation extended by the Singapore Government in taking immediate action to curb the activity.
He said the absence of lorries at night had restored sleep for about 2,000 Mukim Sungai Karang residents after two years of disruption.
"We hope this will not happen again as residents have suffered long enough," he said.
Kampung Simpang Kiri resident Abd Jalil Abd. Manap, 59, said the land reclamation works had also affected the livelihoods of fishermen as the activities were carried out near the river.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BTH: Fair EPF returns and govt's pre-budget statement [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's economy may be growing, with unemployment low and inflation relatively contained.
Yet many Malaysians continue to feel financially squeezed, struggling with rising living costs, mounting commitments and inadequate savings.
The link between encouraging economic indicators and everyday realities was the focus of the latest episode of Beyond the Headlines, with economist Dr Ida Md Yusof and Business Times specialist writer Asila Jalil.
The discussion began with the possibility of a tiered Employees Provident Fund (EPF) dividend, where members with smaller savings could receive higher returns to strengthen their retirement cushion.
However, concerns remain that contributors with larger balances may feel penalised and move their savings elsewhere.
The issue said Ida should also be viewed through the wider public interest, particularly as many Malaysians risk reaching retirement with inadequate savings.
The bigger problem, however, is that many simply do not have enough money left to save. Low incomes, rising costs and growing financial commitments have squeezed disposable income, while easy access to instalment plans and buy-now-pay-later facilities can add to household debt.
The panellists also discussed why official inflation figures do not always reflect lived experience, as spending patterns and cost pressures differ between households.
Separately, other priorities highlighted included better wages, stronger retirement protection, affordable childcare, support for an ageing population and assistance for businesses facing higher operating costs as the 2027 Budget approaches. But with limited public resources, the challenge is not simply to spend more.
The real test is whether Malaysia can turn economic growth into better wages, stronger savings and greater financial security for ordinary Malaysians.
More in the latest episode of Beyond the Headlines. Watch on NST Online's YouTube channel.
